Merges changes to districts from a bunch of different mods. FOR VERSION 2.2 OUTDATED. DON'T USE FOR NOW.

WARNING 1: Depending on the mods you have, additional patches WILL BE required. Only the patches listed as obsolete below are not required. This overwrites any other patches for districts anyway, so it is better to be on the safe side. Think of this mod as a patch to patch your patches.

WARNING 2: Do NOT get this if you use District Diversity or District Overhaul. You don't even need this then. See more below.

NOTE 1: Warnings about modifiers and planet classes can be safely ignored.


Please post all request for new mods for this patch in the 'Mods that mess with Districts' collection linked above.


Not only are mods which change districts incompatible with each other, but so are all mods which add new planet classes, due to the way the districts are implemented. Because of this, these is a large amount of patches available on the workshop which only exist to fix the districts.

The Universal Districts Patch combines all those patches in such a way that it works regardless of which combination of supported mods you are running. This means all mods below are supported, all the time, even if some are missing. One exception to this is that the artificial caps on rural districts have been removed. This means those districts are only limited by the tiles and modifiers of the planet, and that it is possible for planets to have no districts of certain types.

This addon brings the cosmic quadrant in your galaxy view.
The quadrant consist of 4 circles rotating slowly around the galactic core, demarcating 4 different areas:
 - The deep core, uninhabitable and hostile area.
 - The outer core, where life can thrive, but is still very much in the core area.
 - The inner rim, as star density gets lower, we enter the rim area, that's where the sun would be.
 - The outer rim, the remote area where stars slowly give ground to cold empty space. This area is empty for any galaxy < 600 stars.
The quadrant also comes with some measurement, from 0 to 20 kpc (kiloparsec). A 1000 stars galaxy is around 40 kiloparsec in diameter, which a bit larger than our own milky way (~35 kpc), while a 400 stars will be less than 30 kpc.

The original mod is no longer required, but recommended:

Features
The Shrouded Regions: These parts of the galaxy are anomalous dead zones with enormous concentrations of psionic energy. High Zro concentrations, ancient megastructures and ancient threats lurk there. These regions are wounds in the galaxy that won’t heal. (Inspired by Star Wars’s Unknown Regions)

The Galactic Crossing:  An advanced hyperlane network spanning the entire galaxy, serving as a vital route for trade and military movement. The few claimable star systems along it are among the most fiercely contested in the game. Controlling them means controlling the flow of war and commerce. 

Children of Zro - Origin:  New Election Mechanic 
Play as an Imperial Realm, inspired by Dune, and get the Zro Flowing!

Midgame Crisis with an interactive Story: The Sanctuary of Ralis: The Shrouded Regions are not natural. Something caused them - and now, something is trying to escape them. This midgame crisis forces difficult choices, reshapes the political landscape, and sets the stage for what's to come in the aftermath.

A Second Age of Galactic Exploration: In the aftermath of the crisis, new regions of space will be unlocked, bringing the early-game experience of expansion and exploration back into the mid-to-late game. Look for special wormhole-like gates along the Galactic Crossing!

This mod is always one major version earlier than the latest version, as a backup

Newest Version Here [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2529002857]last update of Production Revolution
v2.056 (Check you mod version in the mod panels and always get the latest version for the newest bug fixes.)
Without a doubt, pops and jobs are Stellaris' biggest source of lag right now. Every month, the AI checks, for every single pop in the game, for every single trait and modifier, every single job and its candidate pops. You can imagine how intensive this gets, so much so that Paradox had to introduce population control in the 3.0 update.
What Production Revolution(PR) does is to completely get rid of that system, and condense everything into a single, easy-to-use system. Every pop is aggregated into a variable known as Manpower(representative of population) for every planet, and every job type compatible with this mod is condensed into a single job representative of the output/work of all the jobs on that planet. In short, this means that instead of checking thousands of pops for hundreds of different jobs, Stellaris only needs to do it only once.

[img=https://steamuserimages-a.akamaihd.net/ugc/1655600078953932750/D48042C0DAA25EB11495A228E966D6B2C9A97CAD/]

Overview

Short Description:

- This is a fork of the [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1813104049]Vassals Expanded and Reworked mod by lpslucasps.



New Contract Terms:

- Ruler Designation: Determines whether or not the Overlord can change the subject's ruler. Limited Designation allows the Overlord to choose from amongst the subject's leaders, while Unrestricted Designation allows the Overlord to choose from their own ruler's as well.

- Government Restructuring: Determines whether or not the Overlord can change the subject's government authority (Democratic, Imperial, etc.).

- Domestic Affairs: Determines whether or not the Subject must align their policies with that of their Overlord. Once this is enabled, at that moment, and then every 5 years, the subject's policies will attempt to change to match those of the Overlord.

- Ethnic Affairs: Determines whether or not the Subject must align their species rights (Citizenship Type and Living Standards) with that of their Overlord. Once this is enabled, at that moment, and then every 5 years, the subject's species policies will attempt to change to match those of the Overlord.

- Capital Relocation: Determines whether the Overlord can relocate the capital of their subject.

- Naming Rights: Determines whether the overlord is allowed to rename their subject. -- CURRENTLY DISABLED

Other Features:

- All of the subject interaction features of the mod are handled through a new edict: Manage Subject States.

- You can create Planet-State vassals from individual planets via a planetary decision.

- Changing your subject's name: To do this, I made it so your subject name will change to the name of your Capital system. You can easily rename your capital system, and so, you can easily rename your subjects.

- You can give subjects all of the technology that you have researched.

- Taxes can be more fine-tuned, with separate tax options for each resource, and 5% increments.

- There is a new Casus Belli/War Goal to to steal another nation's subject if the subject is neighboring you. If you win the war, you will be prompted to install a new leader in the subject nation (as this is how it has been done historically, think Rome and Parthia).

--

- Subjects will now get an impact to the stability of their planets and their faction happiness every time something is changed. This is to represent the populace's feeling of resentment at foreign intervention. Loyal subjects will have a lower stability hit, for less time. These effects will not apply for the first two times you change their name/subject type, or the first time you change their authority.




Notes:

- Condiminum can only be made from Subjects who border a nation that is not your Subject.

- You can only have 1 of each type of Specialized Subject (Prospectorium/Scholarium/Bulwark)

- You may only have one Blood Tributary.

- If using my [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2434790082]Civil Wars mod, place this mod after/below it in the load order.

- For the best experience, I recommend [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1623423360]UI Overhaul Dynamic. If you use it, you must place it after this mod in the load order.

- If you have more than 10 subjects and want to manage one, you may have to refresh the edict a few times to get the correct subject to appear on the list.

Adds additional mandates for democratic empires. Now you're not just limited to building mining or research stations.


General Changes
-All mandates give 10 months worth of unity
-All mandates give an additional reward that lasts for 10 years (reward depends on mandate, check your empire modifiers after a mandate is completed)
-Mandates that reward on end of term now also reward on leader death, assuming you have satisfied the mandate's requirements
-Mandates that reward on end of term instead reward when elections start
-Some mandates now have sanity checks that limit when they can show up
-Leadership of factions will occasionally change hands for various reasons
-Democracies may adopt term limits

-Restored the old awoken trait from the Limbo anomaly

Modified Mandates
-Buildings observation posts count towards orbital research mandate
-Building a research district on a habitat will complete the orbital research mandate
-Building a mineral or energy district on a habitat will complete the orbital mining mandate
-Build District mandates now account for additional appropriate districts. Building one relevant ringworld district will complete the mandate
-Build District mandates now also count relevant buildings (such as mineral processing and rare mining buildings for mining districts)
-Industrial districts now count for the Urbanizer mandate
-Voidborn Origin gains access to all district related mandates except farming

New Mandates

Interstellar Expansion
Either colonize a new planet OR expand into 4 new systems

Interstellar Highway
Construct 4 Hyper-Relays (requires Hyper-Relay Technology)

Interstellar Exploration
Completely Survey 6 new systems

Peacemaker
Be involved in no wars by the end of your term

Shipwright
Must be using at least 75% fleet capacity by the end of your term

Uplift Species
Uplift a pre-sapient or pre-FTL species in your empire

Great Emancipator
Ban slavery

Outlaw Robotics
Outlaw both robots and AI

Legalize AI
Legalize both robots and AI (either servitude or full rights)

AI Liberation
Give AI full rights

Aggressive Diplomacy
Set war policy to unrestricted or liberation

Defensive Stance
Set war policy to no wars

Xenopurger
Purge five xeno pops

Army Recruiter
Recruit 6 armies. Buildings and upgrades to buildings that give soldier jobs count as 3 per additional soldier job. Buildings that give enforcer jobs count as 2 per additional enforcer job.

Xeno Alliance
Join a defensive pact or federation

Xeno Isolation
Leave any defensive pacts or federations, break any migration treaties, have accept no refugees policy

Warmonger
Start an aggressive wars

Declare Rival
Declare a rivalry

Open Migration
Sign a migration treaty

Science Without Borders
Sign a research agreement

Individual Freedom
Ban resettlement and population controls, no pops under migration control

Xeno Disenfranchisement
No xenos have full citizenship rights by end of term

Tough on Crime
No planet has more than 15% crime

This is an addon for NSC3 that adds the shipsets from the Mass Effect universe to the game. This mod adds the following shipsets that are available to select for a new game:


[*]Systems Alliance
[*]Turian Hierarchy
[*]Cerberus
[*]Reapers
[*]Geth
[*]Collectors
[*]Reapers/Geth/Collectors
[*]Quarians


IMPORTANT NOTES

[*]Because Frigates and Destroyers use the same hulls in NSC, we had to do a little bit of trickery with the Normandy in the Systems Alliance and Cerberus sets. When using either of these sets, you will see that the Frigate and Destroyer base hulls are blank, and you will be able to choose to use the original Normandy, the Normandy SR-2, or the original Destroyer model depending on which section you choose. There is no way I know of to circumvent this, it's just how it is. Please do not report it as a bug, because it is working as designed.

[*]In addition to the ship models added, there have also been changes to other models such as starbases, stations, and similar. Most of the sets in this mod will use the Systems Alliance models, because the original modeler that made all of this did not make species-specific minor stuff like stations and such.

[*]There are no turrets or weapon locators on these models - all weapons will appear to fire from the center of each ship. This is something that will not be changed, as it would require redesigning the 3D models.

[*]I am not a 3D modeler, and we do not have one on the NSC team. This mod is considered complete as it is, except for any future bug fixes or game updates that are needed. I will not be changing any ship or structure models.

[*]There may be a few minor texture errors here and there. I do not have the knowledge to fix these, so I'm afraid that everyone is going to have to live with those minor issues.

PrologThis is a continuation of the outstanding [url=//steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/1491711756]Crisis Manager - Mid-Game Edition by NaK1119.

The Unofficial Crisis Managers are an ongoing, [url=//github.com/TehFishey/stellaris-crisis-managers]open-source project. Note that given the complexity of this mod, not all features have been fully tested in the latest versions. If you come across any bugs, please report them either in the comments below or on GitHub. If you'd like to contribute, or help with bugfixing, code maintenance, or localization/translation, please don't hesitate to PM me or leave a comment!

⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀–--------––----------––--------–

⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀–------–-------––-------–------–

Summary
This mod provides in-game tools for customizing mid-game crisis events, such as the Rise of the Great Khan and several events related to L-Gates. Among other things, it provides options to make these crises more powerful or weaker, to make them happen sooner or happen later, and to alter the probabilities of random events/outcomes (such as what happens after the L-Cluster is opened or after the Great Khan dies).

Although this is sub-mod of the [url=//steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/2558262194]End-Game Edition, this mod works as a standalone as well (though the configuration menu might be a little more awkward to use).

This mod comes with a default configuration template; more are available if you're using the End-Game Edition alongside it.

This Crisis Managers and companion mods (like [url=//steamcommunity.com/workshop/filedetails/2577705378]Sleeper Edition) are kept separate for comparability reasons, but will be merged in the future. If you're looking for even more challenge, consider adding the (standalone) [url=//steamcommunity.com/workshop/filedetails/2038763403]Total War Pack to your game as well.

⚹ Important Note
The deadline for setting parameters of L-Gate events comes much sooner than those for the other crises. Specifically, these settings can only be changed until any empire (AI or player) finds a Gateway or L-Gate. It's strongly advised that you set these parameters at the start of the game.

Requirements
The menu can be accessed in-game through your choice of [url=//steamcommunity.com/workshop/filedetails/1087781345]Mod Menu, [url=//steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/2458024521]Dynamic Mod Menu, or the [url=//steamcommunity.com/workshop/filedetails/2466607238]Infinite Core Framework! If not, you can run it using the console command: 'event CrisisManagerMenu.100'

Features
Players can access the following options via an in-game menu:[*]Configurations for the timings, potential triggers, and fleet power for the Great Khan event chain.
[*]Settings for changing the number of times the Khan can reincarnate, and enabling reigning of multiple Great Khans.
[*]Configurations for what is able to happen after the Great Khan dies.
[*]Configurations for the requirements and potential outcomes for opening the L-Gates.
[*]Configurations for the fleet power and capabilities of the various entities that may spawn from the L-Gates.
[*]Options to manually trigger L-Gate opening and the Great Khan's rise, and to end their related crises.
[*]Options for manually adding or removing L-Gates (Warning: this can be UNSTABLE).
[*]More things…

Several preset templates for all of the above settings are included with the End-Game Crisis Manager mod. Additionally, user-designed template presets can be built as custom mods/addons; instructions for doing so can be found in the End-Game Crisis Manager's directory.

Installation / Uninstallation
This mod should be installed for new games (but still works, just with less functionality).
This mod can be uninstalled safely only when all of following conditions are satisfied:
• Horde Crisis is NOT ongoing
• Gray Tempest is NOT ongoing
• The Dessanu (an empire that might spawn from the L-Gates) do NOT exist

Localization / Languages
• English 🇺🇸 (may need some improvement)
• Русский 🇷🇺 Аргокон Эстейл

If you would like to help with editing or UI cleanup, or translate Crisis Manager into your language, please let me know in the comments or a DM!

Compatibility
✅ probably COMPATIBLE with mods modifying AI, ships of Horde or Gray Tempest
✅ probably COMPATIBLE with ZoFE 4.0
✅ COMPATIBLE with [url=//steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/2028826064]A Deadly Tempest – thanks to the hard work of FirePrince
✅ COMPATIBLE with [url=//steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/2508704523]The Great Khan Expanded
❎ probably NOT compatible with mods modifying Horde Crisis, Marauders before Great Khan reigns or L-Gate events.

If there are any compatibility issues you are especially interested in, leave a comment.

To-Do / Planned

• Can manually spawn different L-Cluster outcomes even if an outcome had already spawned. (partial hidden beta in)

Features: 86 Pre-Scripted Empires+
This mod vastly expands on the selection of stock pre-scripted empires, offering a wide range of carefully designed and thematically consistent factions to populate your games. When starting a new game, Stellaris will randomly choose empires from the roster to seed throughout the galaxy.

For the content-enriched non-achievement compatible version of this mod, see [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1380773790]Just More Empires (Expanded). Use one or the other, not both.

The random number generator (RNG) is an amazing part of Stellaris, making it possible to never encounter the same galaxy twice. If, like me however, you prefer fewer of the zany totally random creations like peacock hive minds and GEICO gekko fanatic purifiers in favor of somewhat more familiar sci-fi archetypes, then this may be the mod for you!

Almost all of the possible government types in Stellaris are represented in the roster at least once, and I took care to equitably distribute species traits and civics to reduce a sense of same-ness. Regardless of your empire's ethics, the chance of encountering a hostile neighbor is as good as encountering a friendly one when playing in a Just More Empires galaxy. Homeworld types are also balanced so that all nine types of habitable planet have nearly equal representation.

There are also ten different Earth-based empires in this mod, but only one will appear in any game (none will appear as an AI if you start on Earth as the player). Will you encounter the freedom-loving Earth Colonial Administration? The xeno-hating Divine Terran Crusade? Or perhaps the post-communist Revolutionary Union of Sol? 

You will also find five different Deneb-based Human empires, themed as alternative stories to the canon Commonwealth of Man's colonization of that system. These alternative Denebs work in the same way. Only one can appear in any galaxy. This makes for a great number of possible Earth/Deneb combinations for lots more variety in your human-to-human interstellar politics.

Compatibility: Near Universal
This should be inherently compatible with all DLC. In order to play as or in a galaxy with the Humanoid or Plantoid empires in this mod, you'll need to own the relevant species pack DLC. You'll need the Utopia expansion to play as or in a galaxy with any of the empires that have the Syncretic Evolution civic. You'll need Synthetic Dawn for the machine empires. You'll need MegaCorp for the megacorps. Of the entire roster, however, about 60% require no DLC or expansions at all, so you're still getting over 40 pre-scripted empires for a totally vanilla copy of Stellaris.

Mods that make significant changes to default portraits, traits, ethics, and civics may break Just More Empires. Mods that only add to these defaults, such as Planetary Diversity, will probably work with it just fine. In its achievement compatible form, I'll only guarantee JME's compatibility with other achievement compatible mods.

[h1Alternative Implementation

If you prefer granular control over which empires spawn, drop the contents of this pastebin https://pastebin.com/Fu0epmpL into your user_empire_designs.txt and disable the mod.

If you enjoy this mod, please rate it positively and favorite it so others can find it more easily.

[url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2465121344] Tactical Menacing Sections 

Tactical Ship Sections aims to widen the options given by ship design choices, without creating additional ship classes, to maintain an aura of vanilla likeliness and balance.

Major Changes

Vanilla Hull Upgrades now unlock new ship sections 
Always wondered about a destroyer with strike craft capabilities?
Want to sacrifice some weapons in the design to put more armor/shields?
Corvettes with a Large weapon slot? Checked.
Destroyers and Battleships AND Titans can also have missiles now.

You can do that with the new ship sections.

Major rework on most vanilla ship sections
Every ship have some kind of specialization that you can pick, or simply ignore, being the following:
 Corvettes:  Small weapons 
 Destroyers:  Point defense
 Cruisers: Missiles
 Battleships:  Strike Craft
 Titans:  You need to research Advanced Titan Hulls for this one.  It's Extra-Large Weapons.  

 Destroyers  Get an additional auxiliary slot for extra versatility.

Localization Patches:
[url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1670045745] русский / Russian 
[url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1349012702] 日本人 / Japanese

Adds hard-mounted power stations to all military ships
It never made much sense to me that the ships didn't have built-in power plants!
So this mod adds a fixed power station mount to all military-class hulls, including the military stations :-)

Built-in support

[*][url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=725596168]Realistic Ships!
[*][url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=683230077]New Ship Classes & More
[*][url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=720237457]ISBS: Doomsday Weapons & Ships (after he publishes the next version)!
[*][url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=790455347]Advanced Ship Behavior Modules
[*][url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=702164152]TFW's Bunch of Ship Parts (reactor types, also his standalone reactor mod)
[*][url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=741930256]Star Wars Empire Ships
[*][url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=796529957]Star Wars Rebel Ships
[*][url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=786691625]Board That Ship!
[*][url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=787237693]Stellar Expansion - Voidcraft
[*][url=http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=826432049]Extra Ship Components


I do not read comments or forums on Steam any more. I can only be reached on Github.

To add support for your ship(s) in this mod, you need to provide me with:
1. The ship_sizes identifiers of your ships ("corvette").
2. How many S, M, and L utility slots are present in a standard layout for each ship type. If the number is different depending on section types, I need an average number. For vanilla Battleship, it's 0, 0, 10. For Cruiser, it's 0, 6, 3.
3. The entire mod (almost) is generated by a script that you can find in the "generate" folder in the mod ZIP. It's called gen.lua. Should be easy enough to understand, so read it. And if you do not understand, you can learn how. Because you are on the internet.
4. Find me on Discord.

To add support for different reactor types, it's a bit more complicated, and depends on the load order of the mods. If your mod loads after this one, it's much easier. Find me on Discord for that, too.

Mod details
The power station mount can be equipped with predefined reactors for every standard (vanilla) tech, from Fission to Zero Point (and the new secret one!).

Power Stations generate ~50% of total hull utility slot capacity, so they free up lots of slots for other parts :-)
Mineral cost remains identical to slot-based reactors.

The AI uses the power stations.
Any non-standard country does not, however. This includes Fallen Empires, Unbidden, Swarm, Awakened, Guardians, Drones, Pirates, Clouds, Wraiths, and everything else where the designs of their ships is predetermined.
However, these countries get significant buffs to a wide array of ship properties if you simply select Hard/Insane difficulty.

This mod does not remove any utility slots. You can still use power reactors in utility slots as before.

Compatibility
Incompatible with anything that changes the default ships. Because Paradox.
I've seen several mods on the workshop that replace vanilla files for no good reason, and also one that actually included all files from Stellaris, thus replacing the whole game! So, please be careful :-)

Compatible with Crystallis Ship Modules.

It is compatible with existing save games, but you need to research something (anything, research any technology) before you get access to previous power station levels.
After that, you get access to higher power station levels along with the core reactor research options.

Please, before you comment with any bug reports, realise that this addon is in fact extremely simple. The only thing it adds is a component.
If you have a problem, it is most likely caused by some other addon.
Or, you're using more than one addon that overwrites 00_ship_sizes.txt.

Replaced files
The mod replaces the following game files:
common/ship_sizes/00_ship_sizes.txt

translations.description_clean:
■ Last Updated: 4.4
- Added an initial leader group selection system. Triggered via a first-month edict, easy to use — full customization and expansion guide available in the mod root directory.
- Updated a large number of leader portraits, with more to come. Low-quality old assets will gradually be replaced with AI-generated artwork.
- Added a new origin, as well as a curator trait ascension feature tied to technology. Rebalanced various old traits and civics.
- This mod only adds content around the vanilla stuff of Stellaris, suitable for players who like anime moe stuff and Touhou things but do not want overpowered or other crazy things. 
It maintains good balance and compatibility. The added content like trait origin civics, their art and text style are close and compatible with vanilla. If you prefer many new settings or OP options and items, it is recommended to combined with other mods to modification.
# This is a self-use sharing mod.

= About character portrait codes: match the file names, for example: "D2" → Ibuki Suika =

■ Will you consider adding more gameplay-related elements? Such as technologies, equipment, and character events, etc.?
I'm tired. Although I got many ideas before, as the saying goes, it's easy to dig a hole but hard to fill it. I also have a certain degree of balance obsession and don't want to waste time cleaning up after Paradonks' done in every version. I'll_try_harder_in_next_life.jpg

■ Compared to similar or like mods, what are the special features of this thing?
* This mod strives to maintain the character portraits display ratio, making it look more sizable, appropriate and coordinated, without the situation like forcibly stuffing the entire portrait into the avatar frame. Portrait images are mostly randomly selected, and most character portraits are of good quality, but style differences are inevitable.
* Includes high-completed namelists pack, without crude and strange character names. it got well blended the elements of fantasy and realism, the number of the names is very large.
* Retains the vanilla gameplay, balance, and compatibility. Including traits, civics and origins style and strength are close or based on vanilla Stellaris, without any numerical inflation or crazy attribute explosion.

■ What elements included in the character portraits?
Mainly from Touhou Project + WarshipGirls (including WSGR and Azur Lane), as well as some other miscellaneous character portraits in anime moe style, with a total of more than 500. All resources are from the internet. And the copyright of all artistic works belongs to their copyright holders.

■ What content is included for settings except the portraits and species?
5 Origins  
31 Civics
34 GSKC flags and emblems with various elements  
15 species traits (including Cyborg Ascension modify traits)  
140+ leader traits (Paladoks standard)  
20+ Council Positions
1 Council Agenda
They are unique, balanced, well-looked, and versatile.
All added content fits vanilla Stellaris well. You can do many customized RP settings around them.
The text of them are very broad, and even using in random countries, they are still not out of place.

* The overall attribute intensity of civics and origins is between T0 and T2.

■ Why mix Touhou with other heretical elements together?
Well, aside from the well-known few, we definitely need some generic faces(Aren't we all generic faces?), right? By a stroke of luck and considering the quality, I chose those, but just their appearance, to fill the Gensokyo Clans Members.
And it's not like we only need those few minorities to carry all the show. Sometimes, we can also exercise our imagination and try out new settings, new choices.
(You certainly understand what I mean, don't beat me for this...)

■ I understood those reasons, but why still mix with other heretical elements?
Because Touhou is Confucianism, and that was a Mandate of Heaven to absorb and integrate others...!
Maybe...

■ I understood all above, but I still can't accept what you said.
How terrible.

■ Other Notes
* Random AIs will not use the species portrait group from this mod. Unless you chose to spawn one.
* Major version update may cause character portraits become disordered, and there is currently no perfect solution about this.
* May file-conflict with the humanoid race mods, but can be easy solve by adjusting the mod loading sequence in your playlist.

That is all.
If you find this thing helpful to you, please leave a favorite or like.

Wish us luck and peace.

[*]Fixes "Features": Corrects a huge amount of various bugs, we or others found.
[*]Performance: Up to 15%! (without trigger tricks or timer tuning, even as we've added many more on_action elements and the existence of the very nasty mod-add bug)–tuned script logic, cleanups (merging) AI_weights and modifiers, using modern syntax as intended, sorting triggers after priority 
[*]Localisation: some open reported fixes (for all languages).
[*]Some AI Improvements: Adjustment of some AI weighting modifiers in certain cases.
[*]Creates a Base for Modding (Silences the error.log): Fixes spam so you can find *real* errors (like from your other mods).

Creating these bug fixes is a lot of work, but listing and documenting them is another level of effort. Therefore, due to the sheer amount, each bug is usually self-explanatory in the code and marked with "# Vfix" (~2500–not counting every minor one).

Compatibility

Star Wars: New Dawn is a total conversion mod set in the aftermath of Revenge of the Sith, spanning the rise of the Empire and the Galactic Civil War. The mod  provides a full overhaul to Stellaris with handmade events, expanded mechanics, and lots of brand new content.

Play any of dozens of iconic Star Wars factions. Will you crush dissent as the Empire, save the galaxy as the Alliance, or start as an underdog and carve a story all your own? 

Languages:
English with community created translation add-ons (Spanish/German/Chinese/Russian, see below)

Major Features

The Galaxy:
New Dawn is set on a handmade galaxy map at four different sizes each with meaningful customization options. 

A story or a sandbox:
Play in the full Star Wars universe following the story as it unfolds, or play sandbox mode in the Star Wars setting.

Ships:
Unique shipsets covering all countries, featuring Galactic Empire, Rebel Alliance, Mandalorians, Confederates, and Chiss designs.

Species:
Over 100 custom species ranging from the iconic Bothans, Ewoks, Hutts, Twi’leks, and Wookiees to the often overlooked Arcona, Ishi Tib, Kubaz, Tiss'shar, and Vagaari.

Events:
Dozens of new events, dig sites, and crisis chains including:

[*]The Galactic Civil War. Rebel raids, Imperial operations, Mandalorian clan conflicts, and the rise of the Empire.
[*]Hidden formable countries.
[*]The Mandalorian Civil War mid-game event chain
[*]Imperial and Mandalorian Crusader player-crisis paths. 
[*]The Yuuzhan Vong invasion.


Featured Mechanics

Rise of the Empire:
The Republic, victor of the Clone Wars, is gone. In its place rises the tyrannical Empire, which demands submission from all. The game begins at this pivotal moment. The Empire needs to consolidate its power, the voices of freedom need to find their strength. Play or watch as the Galactic Civil War unfolds through subjugation, intrigue, and finally, total war.

Institutions provide new ways to influence or interfere with your neighbors, as well as bring prosperity to your empire through various means:

[*]Gaining unique building options for certain empires like COMPNOR Arcology for the Galactic Empire or the Mandalorian Recruitment Center for the Mandalorians.
[*]Hire Confederate veterans and their fleets as the Corporate Sector Authority or fund uprisings in the underworld as the Hutt Council.
[*]And many more!


Tales from the Cantina lead to brand new dig sites and event chains.Track down lost holocrons, forgotten superweapons, and other powerful relics as well as a myriad of new galactic specimens.

Secrets of the Ancients:  Piece together artifacts of legendary civilizations like the Celestials and Rakata to uncover their advanced technologies and rebuild awe-inspiring megastructures from a bygone era.

Ship retirement system allowing players to have greater control of what ships will appear in their rosters. Use it to phase out older Clone War-era designs in favor of modernized designs or simply reduce the amount of variants in the ship designer.

Mandalorian clan mechanic inspired by the Klingon Great House Mechanic from Star Trek: New Civilizations. Mandalorian players can foster relationships between important clans of the Galactic Civil War era such as Kryze, Saxon, and Wren. 

One map, two settings, four sizes each. Play on either the canon map - which starts the player off with preset borders, multiple systems, and access story events - or play on the sandbox map which is a single planet, vanilla-like start.

New megastructures such as Orbital shipyards, XQ2 trading stations, and Tibanna Mining Platforms.

translations.title_en: Ideal System Locator (formerly Arc Furnace System Locator +)
translations.description_clean:
This mod was formerly named "Arc Furnace System Locator +".

Trouble figuring out the best system to build your kilostructures, stations, or branch offices in while playing Stellaris? This mod will help!

[url=https://www.paypal.com/ncp/payment/ELGMG24PFFSNA]Like this mod? Donate here!

Mod Effects:
Adds an "Ideal System Locator" decision to your capital planet once you've unlocked the ability to build one of the supported megastructures or starbase buildings. This creates an event pop-up with options to search for the following:

[*] Minor Megastructure Notification Settings: Options to enable notifications for when you build/upgrade a Hyper Relay, Arc Furnace, or Dyson Swarm
[*] Waystation: Up to 20 systems with the best value for a nomadic waystation, in a selection of total value, operational reserves, and best per resource.
[*] Branch Office: The top 5 colonies whose owner you have a commercial pact or federation with which will give you the most trade value from a branch office.
[*] Arc Furnace: The top 5 systems which will get the most deposits added if you build an Arc Furnace in them.
[*] Dyson Swarm: Up to 7 stars with the largest energy or research deposits for a Dyson Swarm, plus the star with the largest deposit of each other resource if you own a star with it. (Note: Due to scripting limitations, this function is only capable of evaluating deposits that exist in the base game. If you're running a mod that adds larger star deposits, it won't see them.)
[*] Central Habitat Complex: Up to 8 systems which will get the most districts of various types if you build a habitat in them. (Note: Due to scripting limitations, this function is only capable of evaluating deposits that exist in the base game. If you're running a mod that adds special orbital deposits, it won't see them.)
[*] Nanite Harvester: The top 5 systems which will get the most deposits added if you build a Nanite Harvester in them. (Note that this is not necessarily the same as the ones that will produce the most nanites/ships when they reach full potential.)
[*] Ice Mining Station: The top 5 systems which will support the most Expand Planetary Sea decisions if you build an Ice Mining Station in them.
[*] Quantum Catapult: The 5 systems closest to your capital that you can build a Quantum Catapult in.
[*] Pyroclastic Resonator: The top 5 systems which produce the most energy if you build a Pyroclastic Resonator in them.


Exactly which system is the best may still partially depend on what deposits they already have, but this makes finding your top contenders much easier.

 

This mod is a simple quality-of-life utility with no gameplay changes or script overwrites, so it should be compatible with all other mods (unless they change how any of these structures work). It can also be safely added to, or removed from, ongoing games.

This mod is not* achievement-compatible. *(At least not while enabled, but since it only evaluates systems without changing anything you can copy the save and load the game with the mod, check your systems, and then exit and reload with the mod disabled again if you're willing to fiddle with save files.)

All translations are MTL.

translations.description_clean:
This mod makes spaceports a bit more interesting. It’s a scaled-down version of a bigger [url=http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=933515499]spaceports and forts mod I made, taking all of the new spaceport modules I made for it and a few other bits, but not taking bits which hurt compatibility or might not be what some people want to play. As such, it should be compatible with everything, including AlphaMod+ (I have built in compatibility so higher level spaceports are scaled as mine are). It would presumably also work with other spaceport module mods, but I can’t promise there won’t be overlap (multiple modules doing the same thing).
It does the following:

-Adds 9 new buildable spaceport modules (along with technologies to unlock them).

-Rebalances existing ones, often making them more impactful but more expensive (as one can only have six of them, but 25 buildings on the planets).

-Creates a new weighting system to help the AI build the right modules at the right time (so defensive ones near borders with hostile empires, resource-producing ones when they lack that resource, mind control lasers when there is unrest on the planet, engineering bays when they have free spaceport slots, etc). Also generally upped the weights in the hope that the AI will be more likely to build them (Glavius claims so).

-Buffs spaceports a bit (they should be maybe double as strong as in Vanilla or a little bit more, though only from spaceport level 3 onwards), as some elements of the mod are based on spaceports being strong – otherwise defensive spaceport modules are worthless, and you don’t want to invest that much money in something that you can’t stop being destroyed.

-Capital worlds’ spaceports get a special buff via a special spaceport module that is scripted to be spawned in them. It gives a bonus scaled by whether you have unlocked the other spaceport defence modules.

-Adds an ascension perk for spaceport fanatics: Orbital Engineering – gives you the basic spaceport module technologies (except for orbital hydroponics and solar panels, which it requires), and 25% of all advanced ones but ‘Will to Power’, which is a bit of a special case. Also gives you a 50% cut to initial spaceport costs (but not upgrades – there’s no special modifier for that) and spaceport modules.

-Adds descriptions for all (new and Vanilla) spaceport modules.

Here is a summary of the changes to the existing modules and of the new ones:

     -Assembly yards still give -10% build cost (I didn’t implement the 1.8 change)
     -Crew quarters are now 1.5x as costly. They have +15% strike craft attack speed added to them, which is slightly useful, but mainly they are more expensive because you only need one to make massive savings...
     -Engineering bays now increase ship build speed by 15% and cut spaceport module cost by 15%, a well as giving a ship upkeep bonus and increasing ship repair speed by a little.
     -Observatories now also produce 3 physics but no planet science bonus
     -Orbital mind control laser gives 3 unity, but only -50 unrest (Vanilla has -100)
     -Synchronised defences (now 'synchronised weapons systems') are far more effective, and focus on boosting your spaceport’s offensive capabilities.

     -Reinforced Spaceport Defenses: Bolsters your spaceport's defences (i.e. shields, armour and hull hp). Similar amount of impact to the synchronised defences.
     -Planetary Strategic Defense Network: Late-game tech that boosts your spaceport's all-round military ability, roughly doubling it.
     -Advanced Orbital Energy and Farming Network: Late-game tech that basically combines the idea of orbital hydroponics and solar panels, and increases the output to 8 energy and 5 food, costs 800 (it stands to reason that by the time you unlock it your empire can do a lot better than +3 energy/food). Not for machine empires
     -High Capacity Power Generation Nework: Similar to the previous, but produces 12 energy and no food. For machine empires only.
     -Towed Asteroid Mining: Mid/late game tech – tow asteroids into orbit and mine them. +8 minerals, costs 1200. Spawns actual asteroids in orbit, which allows you to rebuild it for engineering research via special projects.
     -Orbital High-Tech Engineering: Mid/late game tech – engineering in space. +2 minerals, +2 engineering, some small bonuses to ships built there. Costs 400.
     -Weather Control System: Mid/late game tech. Manipulate the atmosphere to control the weather. +10% habitability (via a planet modifier), +10% food output, +2 society research, +2 unity. Costs 500. Not for machine empires.
     -Expanded Commercial Port: Mid-game tech. Improves your spaceport's ability to facilitate galactic trade. +3 minerals, +10% planetary minerals. Costs 350.
     -Universal Assembly Yard: Late-game tech. Allows all ships to be built faster and for cheaper (this stacks with other modules for specific ships). Costs 800.
     -Orbital Research Institute: Late-game tech. +2 of each science resource, +15% planetary science output

Bring more life to the galaxy, kinda like living systems does.
This mod is a merged continuation of [url=//steamcommunity.com/workshop/filedetails/1320353502]Pirate Waves 3 (+[url=//steamcommunity.com/workshop/filedetails/1365414074]Marauders edition) by ScepraX (+[url=//steamcommunity.com/workshop/filedetails/2357819662]Realistic Pirates by Maltheal), modded [url=//steamcommunity.com/workshop/filedetails/1824241724]Pirate Republic by lpslucasps and [url=//steamcommunity.com/workshop/filedetails/2178781283]The Outer Bulwark (Beta) by Obscuris.


Pirate Waves
This mod spawns pirate fleets dynamically (continuously and endlessly). Every once in a while a pirate station and fleet will appear at an asteroid, barren or habitable planet, usually in some part of the galaxy that’s not owned by any country. The pirate fleet will venture out into the galaxy, raiding solar systems belonging to countries and setting up new pirate stations. Each pirate station will produce a new pirate fleet and disappear 10 years after being build.

How strong the fleets are depends on the difficulty level chosen and the time that has passed in the game. The pirates will start to appear 10 years into the game. If the fleet power of the country closest to where the pirates appear is inadequate compared to the pirates, the power of the fleets spawned will drop.

You can set the difficulty of this mod as well as the interval at which a new pirate station and fleet appear using the settings. With it, you can also disable the creation of new pirate stations and fleets.

Includes a pirate kill counter event in your situation log, containing an overview of the interaction with the pirates. This will appear after encountering them for the first time.

Settings
To set the probability of appearance, you can use the "Pirate Waves" settings via [url=//steamcommunity.com/workshop/filedetails/2458024521]Dynamic Mod Menu or Edict (if not present). The minimum chance is 1% (averaging 1 pirate fleet every 100 months) but you can increase this to up to 100% (averaging 1 pirate fleet every month). Default chance is 5% (averaging 1 pirate fleet every 20 months).

You can use the "Pirate Waves Difficulty" settings to set the power level of the fleets. This will also limit the maximum amount of ships the pirate countries can manage.

The difficult settings are also applied to Marauders, Privateers and the Pirate Republic (only after the game runs 10 years).

Multiplayer
In a multiplayer game, the spawn settings of a random player who has not disabled spawning will be used. If all players except one disable the mod, only the settings of that player will be used. From the difficulty settings, the lowest will be used.

Disabling
The Pirates Waves can be deactivated via menu settings, there are options for several factions available.

If you decide to disable this mod in the game loader or unsubscribe the mod, some existing pirates spawned with this mod will no longer move. Your situation log will also contain a corrupt entry where the kill counter was.

Compatibility
Compatible with savegames.
✔️ Should be compat with most mods (as [url=///steamcommunity.com/workshop/filedetails/2604437397]merger_trigger are used), some mods might influence the gameplay if they modify the pirate ships.
✔️ NSC3 must be below

Why does this mod appear?

For a long time, scientists seem too flat for the moment. Every time people usually go for "Spark of Genius" scientists with high skills, because of flat Research Speed is a king above all.
( And let's not forget those who gained Substance Abuser during their brave survey missions, be proud of their accomplishment pal, good for him/her )
So here we are!
---
What is this?

This mod adds the following features for every Scientist in the game:

[*]Survey Corps:
A policy, there are 6 Survey Corps for scientist folks. These "Survey Corps" give Empire's research points or resources when your Scientists perform successful survey missions, similar to "Databank Uplinks" before it changes.

[*]Research Corps:
Every scientist has one Research Corps, but it will remain as "locked" until skill level 8.
Once unlocked, their Research Corps can start to provide bonus such as "+5% Research Speed".
As long as scientists with their own Research Corps are a part of the council, your Empire will gain Empire-wide bonus.

[*]3 Research Status:
Physics, Society, Engineering.
Level from 0 to 100, they determined how good your Scientists are when they're hired.

[*]Eureka Status:
For every scientist who's leading as the Head of Research, once the status reached 100%, grant six month of research points and a tech option (Based on their research traits).
The progress of the status is decided by their corresponded research level skills, as well as their leader and species traits.

translations.summary_zh_current: 全面扩展科学家养成：勘察军团、科研军团、三级科研状态与尤里卡系统，适配 4.4+。
translations.description_zh_current:
SLE（Scientist Level Extension）是一款针对科学家养成体系进行全面扩展的 MOD（适配群星 4.4+）。作者认为长期以来科学家角色过于扁平——人人都只追逐高技能「天才火花」，本 MOD 通过新增多套成长系统，大幅拉长科学家的养成曲线与培养策略。
• 勘察军团（Survey Corps）：一项政策，共 6 种军团；科学家成功完成勘察任务时为帝国提供科研点或资源。
• 科研军团（Research Corps）：每名科学家拥有一个，技能 8 级前保持锁定；解锁后提供如 +5% 科研速度等加成，携带科研军团的科学家进入议会后全帝国生效。
• 科研状态：物理/社会/工程 3 项，各 0~100 级，决定科学家被雇佣时的质量；尤里卡系统：担任科研主管的科学家状态达 100% 时，发放 6 个月科研点数并基于其科研特质给出一个科技选项。
• 特质兼容：努力做到不阻挡科学家在委任期间获得特质（原版通常最多 3 个，本 MOD 调整了上限）；内置对 Additional Traits、Just More Traits、Xenology: Traits Expansion Reborn 的支持。
• 兼容性：独立运行、不修改原版文件；存档兼容、不兼容成就；本地化含英语、俄语、日语与简体中文。
• 已知问题：原版存在科学家偶尔自我复制、导致科研军团与研究领域等级条失效的 Bug，只能手动删除重复科学家解决。
translations.gameplay_zh_current: 新增勘察军团政策、科研军团系统、三级科研状态与尤里卡机制，科学家成长曲线大幅拉长，雇佣与培养策略更丰富。
translations.reviews_zh_current: 订阅 1.2 万、收藏 2268。这是一款科学家玩法扩展模组，作者自述科学家玩法过于扁平、玩家常倾向追求研究速度与天才火花特质，遂为科学家新增勘探兵团、研究兵团等系统，并放宽其获取特质的限制。作者注明与 Additional Traits、Just More Traits、Xenology 等模组内置兼容，存档兼容但不兼容成就。适配 4.4+。
